top.title: Vintage Ansonia defense, Taylor's big day lead Chargers past Naugatuck for share of NVL title
top.description: Ansonia's Zaire Moore (76) hoists the Shortell-Lucas Trophy with teammates following their win over Naugatuck during their annual Thanksgiving Day football game at Naugatuck High School Thursday, November 26, 2026. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) NAUGATUCK - Just in case anyone had forgotten how dominant the Ansonia football program can be, the Chargers issued a reminder Thursday at Naugatuck's Craig Peters Field. Playing with tremendous physicality and aggression on defense and leaning heavily on a supremely talented running back offensively, the Chargers earned a share of the Naugatuck Valley League championship by beating Naugatuck 32-0. Tymir Taylor rushed for 261 yards on 33 carries, including touchdown runs of 1, 2, 19 and 55 yards to give Ansonia a ton of momentum heading into Tuesday's state playoffs. "It means a lot, beating an undefeated team that beat a team (Holy Cross) that beat us," Taylor said. "It definitely means a lot to come here and put those points on the board like we did today. We're looking really good right now, just getting ready for our first opponent." Ansonia improved to 9-1 and will host a Class SS quarterfinal Tuesday, Dec. 1. Naugatuck also finished 9-1 and will host a Class L quarterfinal. Their opponents will be determined when the CIAC releases the official seeds and pairings Friday. Ansonia coach Shane Kingsley said he felt like a great performance was coming from his team from the moment the Chargers stepped onto the field on Thursday morning. "I felt it from the kids in warmups," Kingsley said. "They had that Ansonia look about them. We told our offensive line they were going to have to control the line of scrimmage. We played Ansonia football today. We ran the ball, ran to the football aggressively on defense and tackled, and the results were what we wanted." The result of such focused play was that the outcome of the game never seemed in doubt from the time Taylor scored his first touchdown. The Ansonia defense was unyielding, and the Chargers' offensive line gave Taylor all that he needed to make big plays. "I think Tymir Taylor has become a complete back this year," Kingsley said. "Last year he might've gotten caught on a few of those runs, but not this year. He's breaking tackles at the line of scrimmage, and when he gets daylight, he's gone. He's worked really hard, and I'm happy he's seeing the results." The Ansonia defense complemented him perfectly, shutting down the very talented Naugy duo of running back/QB Qwentarvous Lee and running back Brandon Andoh. Lee finished with 56 yards rushing and Andoh with 50. "From the moment we came in for the pregame walkthru, we were locked in and ready to go," defensive lineman Zaire Moore said. "It was definitely the aggression and the mindset, and the things they'd been talking about over the internet. It was crazy. We just had to show them who rules." top.title: Here are 4 ways OKC Thunder can snap out of current 3-game losing streak
top.description: For two entire regular seasons, the Oklahoma City Thunder never experienced a three-game losing streaks. Now, they've experienced two of those over the last month. Injuries have finally done a number on the once-hopeful title favorite. A month into the Post-D.C.C. (Dub, Chet, Caso) world, they're clinging onto pure survival. For the first time since the Thunder experienced one of the darkest days in their franchise history, their postseason spot is starting to look a little murky to forecast. Once a foregone conclusion, OKC enters Thanksgiving in 11th place in the Western Conference standings. The Thunder started the year an admirable 8-2. Since then, they've lost seven of nine games. The latest painted a similar picture to most of their defeats. They kept it close, but no dice, in an NBA Cup loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves . So, now what? As surreal as it sounds, the Thunder still have 63 regular-season matchups to go. Here are four quick fixes to their current three-game losing streak: Ajay Mitchell becomes more consistent When the Thunder first experienced their season-altering injuries to Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren and Cason Wallace, most penciled Mitchell in as a benefactor. With three of their four best players out, he was pushed to the front of the line. His temporary promotion includes him going from a Sixth Man to OKC's second-best scorer. So far, it's been a wild ride. Before he dropped 25 points over the daunting Timberwolves, Mitchell had struggled in his last handful of contests. He went on a seven-game streak failing to crack 20 points and on poor efficinecy. That obviously needs to change. Out of pure necessity, too. He hasn't taken full advantage of the opportunity in front of him, per se, but has a couple of more months to do so. Start Alex Caruso Sometimes, the biggest solutions are the simplest ones. Even through their dire health situation, the Thunder have remained stubborn on Caruso's role. It's been mostly bench-exclusive. Sans one start. Run of the mill for his three seasons in OKC. In that time, he's started four whopping games total. Quite the juxtaposition from what his role was on the Chicago Bulls . But considering the Thunder have habitually fallen behind with slow first quarters, can they afford to keep Caruso in his bench role? I just don't think so. He's a basketball impact deity. There's a reason why all of the advanced metrics absolutely love him. He has an eye-popping plus-33 point swing in his on-off splits. I get wanting to reserve that tsunami number to keep your second unit afloat, but that's irrelevant if you're always behind to start games. top.title: Rafael Nadal reveals what he told his uncle during the rain delay in the 2008 Wimbledon final with Roger Federer
top.description: In 2008, Rafael Nadal and Roger Federer delivered one of the greatest tennis matches of all time. Nadal and Federer met in the Wimbledon final for the third consecutive season that year, and this time the Spaniard came out on top after a thrilling five-setter that lasted four hours and 48 minutes. The match had started at 2 pm local time, but it was in danger of having to be postponed until the next day due to rain delays. A second rain delay occurred at around 8 pm after Federer had rallied from two sets down to force a decider, and when the players returned to the court, darkness had started to settle in. At this point, there was no roof on Centre Court. During that interruption, Nadal had a conversation with his uncle and coach, Toni Nadal, which he recalled in a recent interview with Brut . Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images Rafael Nadal recalls what happened in the 2008 Wimbledon final “For me, the 2007 final of Wimbledon loss, I think helped me to be ready for the 2008 final,” said Nadal. The 22-time Grand Slam champion had fallen to Federer in the championship match at the All England Club in 2006 and 2007. He lost in four sets in 2006, but forced Federer to a fifth set in 2007. Recalling his conversation with Toni in 2008, Nadal said: “I would say, okay, I can lose, but I will not fail. That’s true. I said, okay, no worries. I can lose. Maybe he beat me, but I’m not going to lose. That’s what I told him [Toni] on the last rain delay. “Because I was in a tricky situation. I was two sets up. Then I lost the next two. I lost two match points in the fourth. So the match was not in my way in that moment. But I said, okay, I mean, I am closer than ever to winning Wimbledon. So it’s not the moment to fail. I said to my uncle, no worries. I will not fail. Maybe he beat me because he’s very good, but I will be there all the time.” Having squandered two championship points in the fourth set, Nadal ultimately triumphed 6–4, 6–4, 6–7 (5-7), 6–7 (8-10), 9–7 to hoist his first of two Wimbledon titles. Nadal made a habit of winning throughout his illustrious career, but always dealt with losses well. “In some way, the loss needs to be accepted to play,” he said. “Because when you play, especially when you play in a sport like tennis, that every day is one against the other, one will lose. And maybe it’s you that day. “And especially, even imagine when you play against Federer or Djokovic or these kinds of players. You go on court knowing that even if you play well, you can lose. So it’s not about talking about that or have fear about losing. It’s about, you know, that’s there. But you can’t think about that. You have to think about the things that you need to do to try to win.” Photo by ADRIAN DENNIS/AFP via Getty Images Rafael Nadal discusses his rivalry with Roger Federer Nadal played Federer 40 times on the ATP Tour, with the two recording what was arguably the greatest rivalry in tennis history. top.title: Tiger Woods Legal Setback Is Just Noise Before The Hero Return
top.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Tiger Woods’ apparel brand faces a legal setback just as he prepares for his competitive return, yet the golf world remains ready to welcome him back. Davis Love III confirmed that tour leaders view Woods playing as the best thing for the sport. The 15-time major champion will tee it up at the Hero World Challenge next week in the Bahamas after a long layoff. Woods has not played a tournament since July 2024 at Royal Troon. He underwent back surgery in 2025 and addressed a prescription painkiller addiction earlier this year. Despite these struggles, reports from HITC via Yahoo indicate he has reached “crazy” ball speeds during practice sessions. The tour is eager to see if his body can handle the pressure of competition again. The Tour Needs The Buzz Back PGA Tour chiefs are not hiding their desire to see Woods compete. While speaking on the Fully Equipped Podcast, Davis Love III revealed the sentiment inside the tournament office. He stated, “In PGA Tour talks, you know, talks around our tournament office, the best thing for the PGA Tour, or the Champions Tour, is for Tiger Woods to play.” The tour knows that Woods brings a level of attention no other player can match. Love compared the situation to Michael Jordan’s return to the NBA. “You know, we miss him, we miss the buzz that he gets,” Love said. “You know, Michael Jordan left for a while, and then he came back to the NBA.” This comparison highlights just how much the game has felt his absence over the last two years. The light he shines on other players like Rory McIlroy and Blades Brown is something the tour cannot ignore. A Controlled Environment For A Comeback The Hero World Challenge offers the specific setting Woods needs to test his limits. Love described the event as the ideal spot for a comeback attempt. “The Hero is the perfect place, you know? It’s a controlled environment,” Love said. This setup allows Woods to play without the overwhelming pressure of a full-field major championship. Experts suggest a schedule of about 10 events for Woods in 2027, including the majors. This approach prevents him from pushing his body or mind too hard too soon. The Father Son Classic is another controlled event that could spur him on to join the Champions Tour later.

top.title: Levski Sofia coach says Marseille fan clashes 'unacceptable'
top.description: A blood-stained Levski Sofia supporter tries to escape from Marseille supporters ahead of the Europa League match (Justine MEDDAH) Levski Sofia coach Julio Velazquez said violent clashes between fans of the Bulgarian club and Marseille supporters ahead of their Europa League game on Thursday were "unacceptable for football". The lead-up to the match at the Stade Velodrome was marred by incidents in the stands between the two sets of supporters, including the throwing of projectiles and flares. Several Marseille fans ran from the stand where they were situated about 10 minutes before kick-off, appearing to pursue a group of Bulgarian supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, where around 500 Levski supporters were gathered. Security personnel eventually managed to restore calm as the game kicked off on time. "It's a very regrettable episode -- these are incidents which are unacceptable for football," said Velazquez. "I support the fans who were caught up in this incident. I hope nothing serious has happened. I'm very saddened by this situation." Ligue 1 club Marseille said it was "working to understand the precise circumstances of these incidents". There were a few further flare-ups between the fans, notably during the half-time break. "We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable," said Marseille coach Bruno Genesio. The home team went on to win the game 1-0. stt/jc/nf

top.title: Ohio State football loses commitment from 5-star defensive end DJ Jacobs
top.description: Ohio State has lost a verbal commitment from DJ Jacobs , a five-star defensive end who is considered one of the highest ranked prospects in country in the recruiting class for 2027. Jacobs told On3 on Nov. 26 that he had decommitted from the Buckeyes. He had been committed for nearly a year. The decision comes six days before the start of the early signing period, which begins on Dec. 2 and allows prospects to solidify their plans. Jacobs is the No. 2 overall prospect and top-ranked edge rusher in his class, according to composite rankings from 247Sports. He had 95 tackles and 12 sacks this year as a senior at Blessed Trinity Catholic High School in the northern Atlanta suburb of Roswell. Georgia, Miami and Tennessee have all been linked to Jacobs late in this recruiting cycle. His father, David, was a defensive lineman at Georgia from 1999-2002. The move by Jacobs leaves the Buckeyes with 22 verbal commitments in the class, which was just outside the top-five at No. 6 in the composite rankings behind Notre Dame, Texas A&M, Miami, Oregon Florida on Nov. 26. The Buckeyes have two other five-star defensive linemen who are committed for 2027 between Marcus Fakatou and Wyatt Smith. Joey Kaufman covers Ohio State football for The Columbus Dispatch. Email him at jkaufman@dispatch.com and follow him on @joeyrkaufman on X. top.title: Steelers Owner Makes Major Decision on Mike McCarthy’s Future After Aaron Rodgers’ Rant
top.description: Steelers owner sticks by Mike McCarthy. Getty Steelers take aim at Mike McCarthy. Getty The Pittsburgh Steelers will be sticking with Mike McCarthy as their head coach. The Steelers released future Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers after he was benched and then took shots at head coach Mike McCarthy. Pittsburgh is off to a 6-4 start and is holding onto a playoff spot. Pittsburgh Steelers Owner Sticks by Mike McCarthy Getty Steelers take aim at Mike McCarthy. After Rodgers went on a lengthy rant about McCarthy and why he isn’t a good coach, Steelers owner Art Rooney II is sticking by the coach. Rooney broke his silence on the incident. He spoke to Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Gazette and said he will be sticking with McCarthy as the Steelers head coach. “I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney said . “The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.” Rooney said Rodgers never once said anything about McCarthy and his health to him during his tenure with the Steelers. So, Rooney admits he is disappointed with how Rodgers handled the situation and went public with it all. “I’m disappointed the way it came out,” Rooney said. “We certainly had hopes that he would be successful here, and I thought at times we certainly got on a roll. We had high expectations. It’s easy to say, knowing what I know today, what would I do? But we had a good experience last year, and so I kind of wasn’t expecting it to go this way this year.” McCarthy is in his first year as the Steelers head coach. Rooney Believes McCarthy Protected Rodgers Not only does Rooney plan to stick with McCarthy, but he believes the head coach did a good job defending the quarterback. Rooney believes McCarthy took bullets for Rodgers when the offense was struggling, instead of the blame going to the quarterback. “The sad thing is Mike took some of the bullets for Aaron in terms of some of the plays that were called. Particularly in the red-zone troubles that we had,” Rooney said. “Mike took some of the bullets for things that were going wrong down there. top.description: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Being one of the best scorers in the NBA doesn’t necessarily mean you’re one of the best three-level scorers. Just look at Giannis Antetokounmpo , who’s been putting up 30 PPG for years without needing much of a three-point shot, or Stephen Curry, who can go for 40 points without even touching the paint (though I’d say he’s definitely inside this category). When we talk about three-level scoring, we’re looking at guys who can get their points in three different areas of the court. The first one is inside the paint, whether that’s through post-ups, layups, dunks, or floaters. The second is the mid-range, where we get most of those pull-up jumpers and fadeaways, and the third is obviously scoring from beyond the arc. What makes these guys so difficult to guard is that taking away one shot doesn’t take them out of the game. Go under a screen, and they’ll pull up from three. Play too high, and they’ll get to the rim. Drop your big man too far into the paint, and they’ll get an open jumper from the elbow. For this ranking, we’re looking at scoring production from each area, shooting efficiency, volume, and how good these players are at creating their own shots. We’re also putting more weight on what they’ve been doing this season rather than their glory or reputation, with all stats coming from the 2026-27 regular season. With that in mind, here are the 10 best three-level scorers in the NBA right now. 10. Kevin Durant Points Per Game: 21.5 Paint Scoring: 6.0 PPG Mid-Range Scoring: 4.5 PPG Three-Point Scoring: 4.9 PPG It feels a little weird having Kevin Durant this low on a list like this, considering he’s probably one of the five best three-level scorers we’ve ever seen. But at 38 years old, the Houston Rockets forward is taking just 13.5 shots per game, his lowest volume since coming into the NBA. The efficiency is still there, though. Durant is shooting 50.8% from the field, 39.7% from three, and 88.1% from the free-throw line, good for a 64.9% true shooting mark. He’s also making 55.6% of his two-point attempts, so it’s not like he’s suddenly having problems scoring inside the arc. Durant ranks sixth in the NBA in mid-range scoring at 4.5 points per game, which accounts for around 21% of his entire scoring production. He’s still getting to those same spots around the elbows, shooting over smaller defenders in the post, and pulling up from pretty much anywhere inside the three-point line. The biggest change is how often he’s getting those shots. Durant is attempting only 4.1 threes per game and scoring six points in the paint, with another 6.2 points coming from free throws. He’s getting fewer opportunities to attack the rim and letting guys like Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson handle more of the scoring this year. top.title: Great Britain overcome Germany to make first Davis Cup semi-final since 2019
top.description: Henry Patten and Neal Skupski clinched victory for Great Britain in a difficult tie against Germany to seal passage to the Davis Cup semi-finals for the first time since 2019. It has been an eventful week for Patten, with his doubles partner Harri Heliovaara sharing his shock and dismay at the Briton’s surprise decision to end their highly successful partnership after three grand slam titles together, only a few days after they were crowned year-end world No 1s. Patten will compete with Skupski, this year’s Australian and US Open champion, in 2027 and the pair immediately demonstrated their potential with an assured victory in the winner-takes-all doubles tie against Germany. The pair beat seasoned doubles players Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz 6-2 7-6(6) in Bologna after world Cameron Norrie edged out Jan-Lennard Struff 6-3 3-6 6-2 and British No 1 Arthur Fery was beaten 6-3 6-2 by world No 1 Alexander Zverev . Krawietz and Puetz are the most successful doubles pair in German Davis Cup history having won 18 of their previous 20 matches but Patten and Skupski started brilliantly before edging a tight second set. Earlier on Thursday Norrie battled past the in-form Struff, who is ranked 13 places higher at 39, saving four break points in a crucial game at 2-2 in the deciding set before rattling off 18 of the final 21 points of the contest. Norrie said: “I knew that my match was going to be a really important one, knowing we’re playing against Germany with Sascha Zverev. I knew I had to take care of this one. Norrie dug deep to put GB ahead (Getty) “I tried to be aggressive those two games from 2-1 up and I overplayed a little bit. But I stuck to it in that game at 2-2 being 0-40 down and then I just found my tempo. “I locked it in. I didn’t really remember the end of the match. I made every return, every ball, I was moving him side to side and I could see him struggling.” Fery had lost to Zverev twice this year, in the Wimbledon semi-finals and again in Vienna, and their head-to-head remained lopsided as the German needed just 70 minutes to level the best-of-three tie. Germany boast the top-ranked singles player (Getty) 24-year-old Fery said: “It’s tough. He’s serving so well, hitting hard from the back of the court so not much time from my end to adjust. It’s obviously not easy, just try and do some different things. It feels a little bit like it’s all on his racket. “He’s a style of player that I struggle to play against. It’s positive, I’ve played him three times this year. If you’d told me that on January 1, it would have been a good thing.” GB now face a semi-final tie against Spain, led by Carlos Alcaraz , who beat Austria later on Thursday. Their star player was rested having been lined up to partner Marcel Granollers in the doubles tie, which was not needed after Daniel Merida beat Joel Schwaerzler 6-4 6-4 ​and world No 10 Rafael Jodar edged past ‌Jurij Rodionov 2-6 6-0 6-1.

top.title: Brendan Schaub Tells Navajo Stirling to Leave City Kickboxing
top.description: Brendan Schaub Navajo Stirling City Kickboxing Getty Former UFC fighter Brendan Schaub encouraged current light heavyweight contender Navajo Stirling to leave his gym, City Kickboxing. On Thursday, Eugene Bareman, the head coach of City Kickboxing, said that Stirling will not fight his teammate, UFC light heavyweight champion Carlos Ulberg, for the belt. “Boys from the same gym don’t fight. We’ve had this agreement from the very beginning of the gym. Some things are bigger than fighting. Friendship and the bond you’ve built with someone are bigger than fighting,” Bareman told the media. Schaub thinks Stirling going along with this is a big mistake. Navajo Stirling Making a Big Mistake Taking to his social media, Schaub explained why Stirling is making a big mistake and why he needs to find a new gym immediately. “Navajo needs to find a new gym. Period. A teams ‘code of honor’ shouldn’t stop a young man’s dream. That’s just dumb and Navajo will regret it. What’s good for Eugene isn’t good for Navajo,” Schaub wrote on X . Navajo needs to find a new gym. Period. A teams “code of honor” shouldn’t stop a young man’s dream. That’s just dumb and Navajo will regret it. Was it to just be the second-best fighter in the world, or does he want to be the champion? Right now, it appears that City Kickboxing is protecting Ulberg, which seems to be a mistake given that he is currently injured anyways. While not fighting Stirling is fine for Ulberg, since he holds the belt, it’s not fine for Stirling, because he is a contender and he needs to fight for the belt, which is his ultimate goal in the sport and in life. Right now, the teammates, Stirling and Ulberg, have agreed to not fight each other. But as time goes on, things could potentially change, and Stirling may make a wise decision to leave a gym that is holding him back and realize that he needs to start worrying about himself first and foremost. nigeria.description: With exactly 50 days before Nigerians return to the ballot, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is preparing for a nationwide test that could offer an important indication of whether the country is ready for another fiercely contested general election. On Saturday, November 28, the electoral umpire will deploy its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and electronic results upload technology across 17,676 selected polling units in a mock exercise designed to identify operational weaknesses, test equipment reliability and strengthen public confidence ahead of the 2027 elections. The exercise, scheduled for 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., will cover two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 registration areas, giving INEC an opportunity to assess the performance of its electoral technology across different locations before the presidential and National Assembly elections on January 16, 2027, and the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections on February 6. #OsunDecides2026: Election Officers Take Delivery Of Materials, Mobilise To Polling Units during the Osun State governorship election on August 15, 2026. Chairman of INEC, Joash Amupitan, described the mock exercise as an important part of preparations for the forthcoming elections, while urging Nigerians to participate. The commission’s Director of Voter Education and Publicity, Victoria Meci, explained that the exercise would allow INEC to establish the effectiveness and reliability of its equipment before election day. “We don’t want to wait till the elections before we test the ruggedness, readiness and functionality of the system,” she said during an appearance on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily . According to her, the commission has reduced the accreditation threshold to 850 voters per BVAS device, with additional machines to be provided at polling units with larger voter populations. business.title: Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally The 2019 Lightning conference in Berlin was lit: five hundred “cypherpunks” getting each other high on visions of a future with peer-to-peer electronic cash. Attending a bitcoin conference back in the day felt like being a teenager at a friend’s party while their parents were out of town. It was exciting and new. The feeling was the opposite of FOMO: something big was happening, we were on the inside, and the rest of the world was going to envy us. It was the kind of party that you could only have when the adults weren’t looking. Whenever someone bought a beer (with bitcoin), everyone would hoot and holler and record it on their phones for Instagram/Twitter (it was still called Twitter). Lightning was the bleeding edge. We called it “the Lightning Network” (capitalized, if you please), and talking about it felt like talking about string theory: something so far out you’re not even sure it’s real. I spent a lot of time invoking the abacus . Those are the times some of us remember fondly and keep trying to relive at bitcoin conferences today. That’s why we engage in rituals like drone shows, Satoshi Rockamoto sets, beefsteak dinners , and video game tournaments for sats, but it’s not the same. The ratio of bitcoin OG speakers to suits is shifting. Many event rooms are half empty, and the halls and meeting rooms are full of people negotiating cap tables and profit-sharing splits. The adults haven’t shut the party down, but they have crashed it, and it kinda feels like their party now. The most exciting thing I noticed at the last bitcoin conference I attended was that nothing exciting happened. And that’s worth celebrating. From Tech Subcultures to Mainstream Tech Adoption The road to boring is seldom smooth. Technological innovation benefits from passion and bold ideas. People work harder on a project when they feel strongly about it and identify closely with like-minded collaborators. That’s where tech subcultures, their rituals, and their dogmas come from. But such passion and tribalism feed conflict, at least for a while until the tech goes mainstream, and normies, who couldn’t care less about subculture squabbles, take over. This progression from an exciting new technology that inspires strong emotions to a humdrum utility is not unusual. World-changing innovations often (always?) start with a committed subculture that identifies fiercely with their weird tech before the mainstream adopts it and soon expects it. In fact, this trajectory has become the standard doctrine of tech marketing. For example, in the early days of the internet, early adopters wrote a Declaration of the Independence of Cyberspace , picking a fight with states and corporations despite having nothing to back it up but chatrooms and dreams. entertainment.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
entertainment.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. Then you probably remember that voice. Deep, commanding and unmistakable, it often came with his signature red cap, traditional Igbo attire and a generous helping of proverbs. The actor was just as memorable away from the screen, where his sharp wit, outspoken nature and candid opinions made him a fascinating personality in interviews. He was never one to shy away from saying exactly what he thought, and that straightforwardness became another part of what audiences remembered about him. For generations of Nollywood viewers, Pete Edochie was the actor they could recognise before he had even finished his first sentence. He became one of Nigerian cinema’s most familiar faces, often playing kings, chiefs, fathers and respected elders. His breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart , a performance that helped establish him as one of Nollywood’s most respected actors. The veteran actor passed away in Enugu yesterday, on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, at the age of 79, following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. Quality, affordability, accessibility and the story behind what we wear are increasingly becoming part of how consumers make their choices. entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). sports.title: Rafael Nadal reveals what he told his uncle during the rain delay in the 2008 Wimbledon final with Roger Federer
sports.description: In 2008, Rafael Nadal and Roger Federer delivered one of the greatest tennis matches of all time. Nadal and Federer met in the Wimbledon final for the third consecutive season that year, and this time the Spaniard came out on top after a thrilling five-setter that lasted four hours and 48 minutes. The match had started at 2 pm local time, but it was in danger of having to be postponed until the next day due to rain delays. A second rain delay occurred at around 8 pm after Federer had rallied from two sets down to force a decider, and when the players returned to the court, darkness had started to settle in. At this point, there was no roof on Centre Court. During that interruption, Nadal had a conversation with his uncle and coach, Toni Nadal, which he recalled in a recent interview with Brut . Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images Rafael Nadal recalls what happened in the 2008 Wimbledon final “For me, the 2007 final of Wimbledon loss, I think helped me to be ready for the 2008 final,” said Nadal. The 22-time Grand Slam champion had fallen to Federer in the championship match at the All England Club in 2006 and 2007. He lost in four sets in 2006, but forced Federer to a fifth set in 2007. Recalling his conversation with Toni in 2008, Nadal said: “I would say, okay, I can lose, but I will not fail. That’s true. I said, okay, no worries. I can lose. Maybe he beat me, but I’m not going to lose. That’s what I told him [Toni] on the last rain delay. “Because I was in a tricky situation. I was two sets up. Then I lost the next two. I lost two match points in the fourth. So the match was not in my way in that moment. But I said, okay, I mean, I am closer than ever to winning Wimbledon. So it’s not the moment to fail. I said to my uncle, no worries. I will not fail. Maybe he beat me because he’s very good, but I will be there all the time.” Having squandered two championship points in the fourth set, Nadal ultimately triumphed 6–4, 6–4, 6–7 (5-7), 6–7 (8-10), 9–7 to hoist his first of two Wimbledon titles. Nadal made a habit of winning throughout his illustrious career, but always dealt with losses well. “In some way, the loss needs to be accepted to play,” he said. “Because when you play, especially when you play in a sport like tennis, that every day is one against the other, one will lose. And maybe it’s you that day. “And especially, even imagine when you play against Federer or Djokovic or these kinds of players. You go on court knowing that even if you play well, you can lose. So it’s not about talking about that or have fear about losing. It’s about, you know, that’s there. But you can’t think about that. You have to think about the things that you need to do to try to win.” Photo by ADRIAN DENNIS/AFP via Getty Images Rafael Nadal discusses his rivalry with Roger Federer Nadal played Federer 40 times on the ATP Tour, with the two recording what was arguably the greatest rivalry in tennis history. sports.title: Tiger Woods Legal Setback Is Just Noise Before The Hero Return
sports.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Tiger Woods’ apparel brand faces a legal setback just as he prepares for his competitive return, yet the golf world remains ready to welcome him back. Davis Love III confirmed that tour leaders view Woods playing as the best thing for the sport. The 15-time major champion will tee it up at the Hero World Challenge next week in the Bahamas after a long layoff. Woods has not played a tournament since July 2024 at Royal Troon. He underwent back surgery in 2025 and addressed a prescription painkiller addiction earlier this year. Despite these struggles, reports from HITC via Yahoo indicate he has reached “crazy” ball speeds during practice sessions. The tour is eager to see if his body can handle the pressure of competition again. The Tour Needs The Buzz Back PGA Tour chiefs are not hiding their desire to see Woods compete. While speaking on the Fully Equipped Podcast, Davis Love III revealed the sentiment inside the tournament office. He stated, “In PGA Tour talks, you know, talks around our tournament office, the best thing for the PGA Tour, or the Champions Tour, is for Tiger Woods to play.” The tour knows that Woods brings a level of attention no other player can match. Love compared the situation to Michael Jordan’s return to the NBA. “You know, we miss him, we miss the buzz that he gets,” Love said. “You know, Michael Jordan left for a while, and then he came back to the NBA.” This comparison highlights just how much the game has felt his absence over the last two years. The light he shines on other players like Rory McIlroy and Blades Brown is something the tour cannot ignore. A Controlled Environment For A Comeback The Hero World Challenge offers the specific setting Woods needs to test his limits. Love described the event as the ideal spot for a comeback attempt. “The Hero is the perfect place, you know? It’s a controlled environment,” Love said. This setup allows Woods to play without the overwhelming pressure of a full-field major championship. Experts suggest a schedule of about 10 events for Woods in 2027, including the majors. This approach prevents him from pushing his body or mind too hard too soon. The Father Son Classic is another controlled event that could spur him on to join the Champions Tour later.

sports.title: Levski Sofia coach says Marseille fan clashes 'unacceptable'
sports.description: A blood-stained Levski Sofia supporter tries to escape from Marseille supporters ahead of the Europa League match (Justine MEDDAH) Levski Sofia coach Julio Velazquez said violent clashes between fans of the Bulgarian club and Marseille supporters ahead of their Europa League game on Thursday were "unacceptable for football". The lead-up to the match at the Stade Velodrome was marred by incidents in the stands between the two sets of supporters, including the throwing of projectiles and flares. Several Marseille fans ran from the stand where they were situated about 10 minutes before kick-off, appearing to pursue a group of Bulgarian supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, where around 500 Levski supporters were gathered. Security personnel eventually managed to restore calm as the game kicked off on time. "It's a very regrettable episode -- these are incidents which are unacceptable for football," said Velazquez. "I support the fans who were caught up in this incident. I hope nothing serious has happened. I'm very saddened by this situation." Ligue 1 club Marseille said it was "working to understand the precise circumstances of these incidents". There were a few further flare-ups between the fans, notably during the half-time break. "We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable," said Marseille coach Bruno Genesio. The home team went on to win the game 1-0. stt/jc/nf

sports.title: Ohio State football loses commitment from 5-star defensive end DJ Jacobs
sports.description: Ohio State has lost a verbal commitment from DJ Jacobs , a five-star defensive end who is considered one of the highest ranked prospects in country in the recruiting class for 2027. Jacobs told On3 on Nov. 26 that he had decommitted from the Buckeyes. He had been committed for nearly a year. The decision comes six days before the start of the early signing period, which begins on Dec. 2 and allows prospects to solidify their plans. Jacobs is the No. 2 overall prospect and top-ranked edge rusher in his class, according to composite rankings from 247Sports. He had 95 tackles and 12 sacks this year as a senior at Blessed Trinity Catholic High School in the northern Atlanta suburb of Roswell. Georgia, Miami and Tennessee have all been linked to Jacobs late in this recruiting cycle. His father, David, was a defensive lineman at Georgia from 1999-2002. The move by Jacobs leaves the Buckeyes with 22 verbal commitments in the class, which was just outside the top-five at No. 6 in the composite rankings behind Notre Dame, Texas A&M, Miami, Oregon Florida on Nov. 26. The Buckeyes have two other five-star defensive linemen who are committed for 2027 between Marcus Fakatou and Wyatt Smith. Joey Kaufman covers Ohio State football for The Columbus Dispatch. sports.title: Steelers Owner Makes Major Decision on Mike McCarthy’s Future After Aaron Rodgers’ Rant
sports.description: Steelers owner sticks by Mike McCarthy. Getty Steelers take aim at Mike McCarthy. Getty The Pittsburgh Steelers will be sticking with Mike McCarthy as their head coach. The Steelers released future Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers after he was benched and then took shots at head coach Mike McCarthy. Pittsburgh is off to a 6-4 start and is holding onto a playoff spot. Pittsburgh Steelers Owner Sticks by Mike McCarthy Getty Steelers take aim at Mike McCarthy. After Rodgers went on a lengthy rant about McCarthy and why he isn’t a good coach, Steelers owner Art Rooney II is sticking by the coach. Rooney broke his silence on the incident. He spoke to Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Gazette and said he will be sticking with McCarthy as the Steelers head coach. “I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney said . “The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.” Rooney said Rodgers never once said anything about McCarthy and his health to him during his tenure with the Steelers. So, Rooney admits he is disappointed with how Rodgers handled the situation and went public with it all. “I’m disappointed the way it came out,” Rooney said. “We certainly had hopes that he would be successful here, and I thought at times we certainly got on a roll. We had high expectations. It’s easy to say, knowing what I know today, what would I do? But we had a good experience last year, and so I kind of wasn’t expecting it to go this way this year.” McCarthy is in his first year as the Steelers head coach. Rooney Believes McCarthy Protected Rodgers Not only does Rooney plan to stick with McCarthy, but he believes the head coach did a good job defending the quarterback. Rooney believes McCarthy took bullets for Rodgers when the offense was struggling, instead of the blame going to the quarterback. “The sad thing is Mike took some of the bullets for Aaron in terms of some of the plays that were called. Particularly in the red-zone troubles that we had,” Rooney said. “Mike took some of the bullets for things that were going wrong down there. He tried to protect him, and it just wasn’t working.” The Steelers will now turn their attention to the Denver Broncos on Friday afternoon. sports.title: Cesc Fàbregas speaks on potential Barcelona return
sports.description: Cesc Fàbregas speaks on potential Barcelona return Como head coach Cesc Fàbregas has this week spoken out on the possibility of taking his talents back to his former stomping grounds at La Liga champions Barcelona. Fàbregas and Flick’s contracts with their respective clubs are due to expire in the summer of 2028. The former, meanwhile, has long been earning for himself a reputation as one of European football’s standout up-and-coming tacticians. On the bench at Italian outfit Como, Fàbregas has defied the odds en route to establishing his club as one of Serie A’s leading lights. Boasting Barcelona DNA courtesy of his time spent at La Masia, the former Blaugrana midfielder is in turn considered an almost inevitable future arrival back at the Camp Nou. Speaking during an appearance in front of the media this week, Fàbregas was therefore drawn on this very topic. And the Spaniard went on to provide an in-depth response, as follows: “I’m one of those who live day by day. Thinking about the future usually doesn’t get you anywhere. “I’m from there, I grew up at that club, and I know everyone, but I’ve never liked thinking too far ahead. The times I have, it hasn’t gone well. Life is like piloting a plane; you never know when it’s going to brake. That’s why we have to try to enjoy ourselves. When it’s time to compete, compete; when it’s time to enjoy ourselves, enjoy ourselves; when it’s time to be with family, be with family. I try to be a balanced person within the competitiveness and demands of being the coach of a club like Como, where we are growing, and I have so many responsibilities. “I enjoy it and know how to maintain the high standards to keep growing at this club and, above all, in my job. But like I said, I focus on the day-to-day, because thinking about the future usually doesn’t get you anywhere. sports.description: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Being one of the best scorers in the NBA doesn’t necessarily mean you’re one of the best three-level scorers. Just look at Giannis Antetokounmpo , who’s been putting up 30 PPG for years without needing much of a three-point shot, or Stephen Curry, who can go for 40 points without even touching the paint (though I’d say he’s definitely inside this category). When we talk about three-level scoring, we’re looking at guys who can get their points in three different areas of the court. The first one is inside the paint, whether that’s through post-ups, layups, dunks, or floaters. The second is the mid-range, where we get most of those pull-up jumpers and fadeaways, and the third is obviously scoring from beyond the arc. What makes these guys so difficult to guard is that taking away one shot doesn’t take them out of the game. Go under a screen, and they’ll pull up from three. sports.title: Great Britain overcome Germany to make first Davis Cup semi-final since 2019
sports.description: Henry Patten and Neal Skupski clinched victory for Great Britain in a difficult tie against Germany to seal passage to the Davis Cup semi-finals for the first time since 2019. It has been an eventful week for Patten, with his doubles partner Harri Heliovaara sharing his shock and dismay at the Briton’s surprise decision to end their highly successful partnership after three grand slam titles together, only a few days after they were crowned year-end world No 1s. Patten will compete with Skupski, this year’s Australian and US Open champion, in 2027 and the pair immediately demonstrated their potential with an assured victory in the winner-takes-all doubles tie against Germany. The pair beat seasoned doubles players Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz 6-2 7-6(6) in Bologna after world Cameron Norrie edged out Jan-Lennard Struff 6-3 3-6 6-2 and British No 1 Arthur Fery was beaten 6-3 6-2 by world No 1 Alexander Zverev . Krawietz and Puetz are the most successful doubles pair in German Davis Cup history having won 18 of their previous 20 matches but Patten and Skupski started brilliantly before edging a tight second set. Earlier on Thursday Norrie battled past the in-form Struff, who is ranked 13 places higher at 39, saving four break points in a crucial game at 2-2 in the deciding set before rattling off 18 of the final 21 points of the contest. Norrie said: “I knew that my match was going to be a really important one, knowing we’re playing against Germany with Sascha Zverev. I knew I had to take care of this one. Norrie dug deep to put GB ahead (Getty) “I tried to be aggressive those two games from 2-1 up and I overplayed a little bit. But I stuck to it in that game at 2-2 being 0-40 down and then I just found my tempo. “I locked it in. I didn’t really remember the end of the match. I made every return, every ball, I was moving him side to side and I could see him struggling.” Fery had lost to Zverev twice this year, in the Wimbledon semi-finals and again in Vienna, and their head-to-head remained lopsided as the German needed just 70 minutes to level the best-of-three tie. Germany boast the top-ranked singles player (Getty) 24-year-old Fery said: “It’s tough. He’s serving so well, hitting hard from the back of the court so not much time from my end to adjust. It’s obviously not easy, just try and do some different things. It feels a little bit like it’s all on his racket. “He’s a style of player that I struggle to play against. It’s positive, I’ve played him three times this year. If you’d told me that on January 1, it would have been a good thing.” GB now face a semi-final tie against Spain, led by Carlos Alcaraz , who beat Austria later on Thursday. Their star player was rested having been lined up to partner Marcel Granollers in the doubles tie, which was not needed after Daniel Merida beat Joel Schwaerzler 6-4 6-4 ​and world No 10 Rafael Jodar edged past ‌Jurij Rodionov 2-6 6-0 6-1.

sports.title: Leeds United Chase French Striker Rennes Could Sell: Is £39m Worth It?
sports.description: Leeds United Chase French Striker Rennes Could Sell: Is £39m Worth It? Leeds United and Everton are reportedly targeting Rennes striker Esteban Lepaul, according to Sport Witness . The 26-year-old France international scored 20 goals and provided five assists in Ligue 1 last season, then added seven in eight league appearances this term, four of them penalties. Rennes extended his contract to 2030 in June, yet the report says they are preparing for a January or summer exit. Transfermarkt values him at €45m, roughly £39m. Eliezer Mayenda, a €22m (about £19m) signing, is struggling, so Rennes are already scouting Rosenborg’s Amin Chiakha as a replacement in attack. Lepaul’s strengths and weaknesses FotMob ‘s data shows a penalty-box finisher. His 29 shots have produced 16 on target and 5.80 expected goals, and he ranks in the 95th percentile among forwards for goals. The weaknesses are just as clear. He wins 40.9% of his aerial duels and 37.8% of all duels, and sits in the third percentile for defensive contributions. Only three of his seven goals this season came from open play. Where Leeds need help Leeds scored only 10 goals in their first ten league games before beating Chelsea 4-1 last Saturday to reach 17 points from 11. Noah Okafor scored twice there and Dominic Calvert-Lewin, 29, converted a penalty, yet the striker missed 19 big chances in the Premier League last season, according to FotMob. Farke’s back three and two strikers need forwards who press, and Calvert-Lewin has led the Premier League for pressures applied since the start of last season. Lepaul’s defensive numbers would test that. Should Leeds United pay £39m for Lepaul? ISTANBUL, TURKEY – AUGUST 2: Anthony Rouault of Rennes interacts with his teammate Esteban Lepaul during the during the pre-season friendly match between Galatasaray SK and Rennes at Rams Park Stadium on August 2, 2026 in Istanbul, Turkey. (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images) No, at least not in January and not at £39m or more. Rennes can keep him in Europa League football on a contract until 2030, and TEAMtalk reports Everton lead the chase. Everton have only Thierno Barry as a senior centre-forward, but Leeds face no such shortage. Their problem is conversion, which makes Lepaul tempting, yet he created just seven chances in 562 minutes and would not help Farke’s pressing. Calvert-Lewin started each of Leeds ‘ first ten league games, and Okafor is scoring, so Lepaul would arrive as a rotation option at a starter’s price. A cheaper, pressing-minded forward would suit the back three better. Summer is the sensible window, when Rennes may have Chiakha in place and Calvert-Lewin’s age gives succession a stronger case. Paying about £39m for 20 goals is fair only if the player can also defend from the front, and Lepaul’s numbers say he cannot yet.

sports.title: Boxing chiefs to assess Fury before Joshua fight following schizophrenia comments
sports.description: The British Boxing Board of Control will assess Tyson Fury ahead of his hotly anticipated bout against Anthony Joshua following comments he made about hearing voices during a mental health episode. A new self-titled documentary about the 38-year-old, to be released on Netflix on Friday, goes into detail about his mental health struggles. He and his wife Paris recalled frightening episodes in which he heard voices threatening him and his family after he was hospitalised with a suspected heart attack in 2016. He said: “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in. It was like the living version of the pits of hell’s fire. I 100 per cent thought I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked and that scared me so much.” In the original version of the documentary, which has since been edited before release, Paris said he was “mild schizophrenic”, although he was not medically diagnosed. Doctors said he had experienced a severe anxiety attack. Paris clarified her comments to The Mirror on Thursday: “Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis. Mental health is complex, and it isn't always easy to find the right words, especially when you're living it with someone you love.” The British Boxing Board of Control said it would evaluate the comments broadcast in the documentary before clearing Fury to box Joshua, with the fight scheduled for 11 December in Cardiff’s Principality Stadium . The board’s general secretary, Robert Smith, told BBC Sport : “We are in the process of dealing with the matter but if there are any medical issues we wouldn't let anyone box, doesn't matter if it's Tyson Fury or not, it could be anybody. “I'm fairly confident he will be absolutely fine. We're dealing with it now and we'll have an answer very shortly. “If our doctors are satisfied he's fit to box, he will box.” He declined to comment on the specifics of the process, saying, “it's a medical matter”. The board’s regulations state that schizophrenia is among psychological conditions which “may preclude” a boxer from obtaining a first licence. An existing licence holder is subject to “such action as in [the board’s] absolute discretion it sees fit”.

technology.title: Microsoft: Hackers in China, N Korea using ARTEX AI tool to break into global tech systems
technology.description: Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hacking crews are among the growing number of groups known for using the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft said this week. ARTEX is an open source, AI-powered penetration testing framework that attackers have adopted to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation since its public release in July. Campaigns that have been linked to ARTEX have targeted cloud environments, IT software like ConnectWise , and financial institutions globally, sometimes reaching privileged access in under three hours. Salt Typhoon is arguably the most recognizable name on the list of ARTEX beneficiaries – the group responsible for attacks on telcos AT&T and Verizon , US government systems , UK prime minister's aides , and more. The lesser-known Crystal Typhoon – the group behind the ArcaneDoor attacks back when Microsoft called it Storm-1849 – was also named alongside it, as were North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Microsoft also named China-state-aligned Storm-0940, linked to the ConnectWise compromise, and financially motivated, Cambodia-based Storm-3358. It had previously reported both groups' use of ARTEX. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of ARTEX in November. GitHub user "Autumn-27" originally published its source code with a Chinese-language interface in July. Various forks of the repo, which was taken down in October, have meant that the same framework is available in multiple languages. According to Infrawatch , there are more than 130 variants of ARTEX in circulation, and it is the most widely used agentic offensive framework (AOF) at present. Like other offensive security tools adopted by criminals, ARTEX can lower the effort required to mount attacks. Experienced groups can also use it to automate repetitive work and pursue multiple avenues at once. As Microsoft echoed this week, after the FBI and AWS issued their warnings earlier this month , ARTEX is proving to be a useful tool for the more sophisticated groups to streamline and hasten their attacks too. It's being used to help attackers steal AI and cloud credentials at "industrial scale," as AWS put it, which provide attackers access to advanced models for free. Microsoft says ARTEX can progress from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access within minutes, depending on its configuration and the target's defenses. "In the past few weeks, we've reported several distinct campaigns that abused ARTEX to search public repositories for exposed secrets, enable supply chain compromise, and scan internet-facing systems for exploitation," its threat intelligence team blogged . "These campaigns illustrate how threat actors use ARTEX to automate various stages of the attack chain. technology.title: Tech's outage problem needs maintenance, not conspiracy theories
technology.description: Years of technical debt, increasingly complex systems, and underinvestment in IT operations have left organizations vulnerable to major outages, according to Forrester. The analyst pointed to a seven-day stretch in November when failures disrupted Microsoft 365, US air traffic control, banking, and other critical services. The coinciding outages provoked "a slew of conspiracy theories about cyberattacks and AI," Forrester said. "The real culprit is tragically mundane: the culmination of decades of technical debt, the frenetic buildout of massively complex and highly interdependent systems, the concentration of risk, and the underinvestment in advanced operations." Forrester urged technology suppliers and in-house IT teams to prioritize resilience as their systems grow more complex. Otherwise, "the tech estate will collapse like a house of cards, taking down consumer and business trust with it." Earlier this month, Microsoft was left struggling to restore many of its cloud services after a core process running on some servers became "overwhelmed" and its attempts to fix the problem failed. Some of its services did not recover for another 24 hours. In October, Google Cloud blamed a "power event" for taking down multiple online products for customers in Western Europe. Affected services included BigQuery Data Transfer Service, Cloud Filestore, Cloud Run, Google App Engine, and Google Kubernetes Engine. In October last year , a major outage impacted Amazon Web Services (AWS), with even Amazon's own web page reported to be offline and dozens of other online services and websites affected. Aviation and banking were also hit this month. A communications outage triggered a nationwide ground stop in the US on November 13 , while incidents involving JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, Apple, Workday, Gmail, and other services added to the sense of widespread instability. "Claims that these were all part of one connected cyberattack or conspiracy are highly unlikely. The real story is much more mundane," the report said . Forrester argued that organizations have prioritized visible improvements over repairs to the underlying technology. "Modernization investments have favored visible change over structural renewal," wrote report authors Lauren Nelson and Mark Moccia. "Organizations routinely fund new customer experiences, cloud migrations, platform consolidation, and AI initiatives because leaders can connect them to growth or productivity. "They are less enthusiastic about updating core systems, simplifying architectures, retiring obsolete components, and eliminating fragile interfaces. The result is a modern front end resting on an aging, brittle, and increasingly interconnected estate." Forrester's recommendations are to map dependencies, test failures and recovery under realistic conditions, and use incidents and near misses to identify weaknesses before they cause another outage. ®

technology.description: Britain's privacy watchdog is getting a taste of its own medicine, with an independent review set to examine the culture, governance, and accountability surrounding the events that led to former Information Commissioner John Edwards' resignation. Karon Monaghan KC will examine whether the regulator's culture and governance allowed problems to develop or made concerns harder to raise. Edwards quit in June after an independent workplace investigation found there was a "case to answer" over his behavior and that his conduct fell short of what was expected of a public official. He disagreed with some of its findings, but ultimately conceded that he had shown "poor judgment." That investigation, however, focused on Edwards alone. According to the terms of reference published on Thursday, it "did not consider the wider conditions in which that conduct occurred, and it was not designed to." The new review will cast a wider net. Monaghan wants to know whether staff could call out bad behavior further up the food chain, and what awaited those who tried. It will also poke around the regulator's leadership and governance arrangements and its relationship with its sponsoring government department, including whether there were adequate ways for concerns to be escalated and those at the top to be challenged. Current and former staff can give evidence confidentially and voluntarily, while Monaghan will be given access to relevant documents and existing material, including staff surveys and data on bullying, harassment and discrimination. The ICO has confirmed it won't use confidentiality clauses in settlement agreements to prevent people from contributing to the review. Monaghan decides which witnesses and documents are relevant, rather than the ICO or DCMS. Access remains subject to legal restrictions, and she must be told when material is withheld and why. She can speak to whoever she thinks is relevant and ask for the complaints, correspondence, and other paperwork she needs. And if that leads her somewhere unexpected, she can ask to widen the investigation. DCMS can refuse, but it won't be able to quietly brush the request aside, and any decision not to expand the scope has to make it into the final report. The review won't reopen the investigation into Edwards, make findings about the conduct of named individuals, or delve into the merits of the regulator's enforcement decisions. Its arrival comes amid a broader shake-up at Britain's data watchdog. The old Information Commissioner's Office was formally replaced by the Information Commission on September 30, bringing with it a new board-led governance model. The government first promised the wider review in July, shortly after Edwards' departure, but it didn't appoint its reviewer or nail down the terms until late November. technology.title: Rackspace pulls plug on Spot cloud service after security breach
technology.description: Rackspace is shutting down its low-cost Spot cloud service after a security breach, giving customers two weeks' notice to move their workloads and retrieve their data. In a notice posted on Tuesday , the cloud computing biz said its Rackspace Spot service will cease operations at 1700 Central Time (2300 UTC) on December 8. Any workloads still running at that point will be terminated, and customers will no longer be able to access their data. "Following the recent security incident affecting Rackspace Spot, Rackspace has made the decision to wind down the service," the company said. "Spot customers are being notified with the wind-down timeline, instructions for retrieving their data and steps to secure their environments." Customers will have to contend with the fallout from the breach while simultaneously trying to get their applications and data off the platform. According to a customer notification seen by The Register , the attackers used leaked credentials to access parts of Rackspace Spot over a period of almost 22 hours on November 17. Rackspace only learned of the intrusion the following day, after a customer raised the alarm. The intruders impersonated legitimate users, created pods in customer Kubernetes clusters, gained access to stored credentials known as Kubernetes Secrets, and listed nodes and storage volumes. "With that access, they could have read any Secret in an affected user's clusters, and any Spot API token or refresh token that user held," Rackspace told customers. Rackspace has since revoked the affected tokens and sessions, removed the pods planted by the intruders, and changed the affected platform and storage keys. Customers must also reissue API tokens, download new Kubernetes configuration files, and rotate credentials stored in their clusters, including database passwords and third-party API keys. Sirish Raghuram, co-founder and chief growth officer of Platform9, which co-developed Spot with Rackspace, shed some light on the root cause in a November 20 GitHub post. "An observability system was breached using a compromised credential," Raghuram wrote. "This was obviously a critical error on our part and we are very sorry we let this happen." Raghuram said the incident necessitated significant changes to the underlying infrastructure clusters, prolonging the outage. Spot's selling point was cheap compute. The service operated an auction-based pricing model, allowing customers to bid for cloud infrastructure at a fraction of the cost of conventional on-demand instances. Rackspace advertised savings of up to 90 percent for customers willing to tolerate interruptions to their workloads. A permanent interruption probably wasn't what they had in mind. Rackspace hasn't explained why it chose closure over recovery, revealed how many customers were affected, or said whether it will offer migration extensions. It did not respond to The Register's questions. ®

technology.title: Wyoming uranium operation shuts down after cyberattack
technology.description: Peninsula Energy has temporarily shut down its Wyoming uranium operation after a "cybersecurity incident" affected plant and wellfield control systems. The Australian uranium producer said on Wednesday that it had activated its response procedures and brought in outside specialists following the attack on its US subsidiary, Strata Energy, which operates the Lance uranium project. Peninsula Energy said it believes the attack is "confined to the plant and wellfield operating and control systems," and that back-office functions, such as payroll and other corporate systems, in both the US and Australia, remain unaffected. "The company's immediate priorities have been to protect the safety of its employees, secure its operating systems, and work towards the restoration of operations in a safe and controlled manner," it said in an update to the Australian Securities Exchange. The notification [PDF] went on to say that Peninsula Energy's investigations into the attack, including whether any data was compromised, remain ongoing. Peninsula has not given a restart date and says it cannot yet assess the impact on its 2027 production guidance. Operations will remain suspended until recovery and safety checks are complete. "Peninsula will provide further updates to the market as material information becomes available," it said. The disclosure of additional information came two days after Peninsula secured a short trading halt, which referenced a cybersecurity incident at its Wyoming site. The November 23 filing [PDF] dated the incident to Friday evening in Western Australia. Wednesday's update clarified that Strata detected it on the morning of November 20, local US time. Peninsula subsequently requested a voluntary suspension of trading until the earlier of November 30 or an announcement on restarting operations and any resulting change to production guidance. Peninsula's Lance project is a uranium mining operation, extracting the element from underground deposits and turning it into uranium concentrate, aka yellowcake or U₃O₈. Uranium concentrate is feedstock for nuclear fuel production, typically undergoing conversion, enrichment, and fabrication into uranium dioxide pellets before use in reactors. The Lance central processing plant was constructed to produce a maximum of 2.0 million pounds (Mlb) of U₃O₈ annually, and is licensed for 3.0 Mlb. Peninsula previously forecast production of 500,000 to 600,000 pounds in 2027, having withdrawn its 2026 guidance earlier this year following operational problems at Lance. It now says it will reassess the 2027 outlook once operations resume. ®
